items.title: Index
items.text: Pytrajopt is an open-source Python library for nonlinear trajectory optimization, built on transcription using direct multiple shooting and collocation, with Pydantic validation to model the optimal control problem and a CasADi backend to formulate and solve the nonlinear program.

items.title: Example
items.text:
To demonstrate how to define and solve optimal control problems with PyTrajOpt, consider the classical Low-Thrust Orbital Transfer problem.

The problem formulation is adapted from Ross et al. ("Low-thrust, high-accuracy trajectory optimization," Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics, 2007). The minimum time reported when solved using the Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto (LGL) pseudospectral method is 47.706 for 300 nodes.

items.title: Problem Definition
items.text:
The state and control vectors for the problem are defined as

\[\mathbf{x}^T = \begin{bmatrix} r & \theta & v_r & v_t \end{bmatrix}\] \[\mathbf{u}^T = \begin{bmatrix} u_r & u_t \end{bmatrix}\] \[ \text{Minimize} ~~ J[\mathbf{x}(\cdot), \mathbf{u}(\cdot), t_f] = t_f\]

items.title: System Dynamics:
items.text: \[\dot{r} = v_r\] \[\dot{\theta} = \frac{v_t}{r}\] \[\dot{v}_r = \frac{v_t^2}{r} - \frac{1}{r^2} + u_r\] \[\dot{v}_t = -\frac{v_r v_t}{r} + u_t\]

items.title: Boundary Conditions & Constraints:
items.text:
\[(r, \theta, v_r, v_t)(0) = (1, 0, 0, 1)\] \[(r, v_r, v_t)(t_f) = (4, 0, 0.5)\] \[-0.01 \le \mathbf{u} \le 0.01\]

(Primal and dual solutions for this problem can be found in the accompanying low_thrust_sol.pdf and results of feasibility checks are provided in low_thrust_feas.pdf

items.title: Installation
items.text: PyTrajOpt uses Poetry for robust dependency management and packaging. You can install the framework directly from GitHub or set it up locally for development.

items.title: Option 1: Install Directly from GitHub via Pip
items.text:
If you want to quickly install the package into your current Python environment without cloning the repository:

pip install git+https://github.com/sandeep026/pytrajopt.git

items.title: Option 2: Install Directly from GitHub via Poetry
items.text:
To add PyTrajOpt as a dependency in another Poetry-managed project directly from the remote repository:

poetry add git+https://github.com/sandeep026/pytrajopt.git

items.title: Option 3: Local Installation for Development (Clone & Poetry)
items.text:
If you want to run the provided examples or contribute to the source code:

  1. Clone the repository: 

    git clone https://github.com/sandeep026/pytrajopt.git
cd pytrajopt

  2. Install dependencies: Poetry will automatically read the pyproject.toml configuration, resolve the dependencies (such as CasADi, Pydantic, NumPy, and Matplotlib), and set up a dedicated virtual environment:

poetry install
  1. Activate the virtual environment: 
    poetry shell

items.title: Multiphase OCP
items.text:
A multiphase optimal control problem consists of \(N_{\text{phases}}\) sequential or interconnected phases, indexed by \(p \in \{1, \dots, N_{\text{phases}}\}\). The framework solves problems of the general form:

\[\min_{\{x^{(p)}(\cdot), u^{(p)}(\cdot), t_0^{(p)}, t_f^{(p)}\}_{p=1}^{N_{\text{phases}}}} \quad J = \sum_{p=1}^{N_{\text{phases}}} \left( \int_{t_0^{(p)}}^{t_f^{(p)}} L^{(p)}(t, x^{(p)}, u^{(p)})\mathrm{d}t + E^{(p)}(t_0^{(p)}, t_f^{(p)}, x_0^{(p)}, x_f^{(p)}) \right)\]

Subject to the following dynamics and constraints for each phase \(p = 1, \dots, N_{\text{phases}}\):

\[\dot{x}^{(p)}(t) = f^{(p)}(t, x^{(p)}, u^{(p)}), \quad t \in [t_0^{(p)}, t_f^{(p)}]\] \[e_{lb}^{(p)} \leq e^{(p)}(t_0^{(p)}, t_f^{(p)}, x_0^{(p)}, x_f^{(p)}) \leq e_{ub}^{(p)}\] \[h_{lb}^{(p)} \leq h^{(p)}(t, x^{(p)}, u^{(p)}) \leq h_{ub}^{(p)}\] \[x_{lb}^{(p)} \leq x^{(p)}(t) \leq x_{ub}^{(p)}, \quad u_{lb}^{(p)} \leq u^{(p)}(t) \leq u_{ub}^{(p)}\]

And across-phase linkage constraints (e.g., state continuity, time coordination, or event conditions):

\[g_{lb} \leq g\left(\{t_0^{(p)}, t_f^{(p)}, x_0^{(p)}, x_f^{(p)}\}_{p=1}^{N_{\text{phases}}}\right) \leq g_{ub}\]

items.title: Transcription: From Multiphase OCP to NLP
items.text: To solve the infinite-dimensional continuous multiphase OCP on a digital computer, the problem is transcribed into a finite-dimensional Nonlinear Program (NLP) by applying direct collocation or multiple shooting independently across each phase while enforcing phase linkage constraints.

items.title: A. Time Grid Discretization
items.text:
For each phase \(p \in \{1, \dots, N_{\text{phases}}\}\), the continuous time horizon \([t_0^{(p)}, t_f^{(p)}]\) is divided into \(n^{(p)}\) intervals of length \(\Delta t^{(p)} = \frac{t_f^{(p)} - t_0^{(p)}}{n^{(p)}}\), generating \(n^{(p)} + 1\) mesh grid points:

\[t_k^{(p)} = t_0^{(p)} + k \Delta t^{(p)}, \quad k = 0, 1, \dots, n^{(p)}\]

(Note: For sequential phases, the final time of phase \(p\) typically coincides with the initial time of phase \(p+1\), i.e., \(t_f^{(p)} = t_0^{(p+1)}\).)

items.title: B. NLP Decision Vector (\(W\)) Structure
items.text:
The continuous functions \(x^{(p)}(t)\) and \(u^{(p)}(t)\) for every phase are parameterized by state values at the grid nodes and control values over intervals. The global NLP decision variable vector \(W\) is assembled by concatenating the free time variables, state matrices, and control matrices across all phases:

\[W = \begin{bmatrix} T_{\text{free}}^T & \text{vec}(X^{(1)})^T & \text{vec}(U^{(1)})^T & \dots & \text{vec}(X^{(N_{\text{phases}})})^T & \text{vec}(U^{(N_{\text{phases}})})^T \end{bmatrix}^T\]
  • Time variables (\(T_{\text{free}}\)): Includes all free initial, final, or duration times across the phases (e.g., \(t_0^{(1)}, t_f^{(1)}, t_f^{(2)}, \dots, t_f^{(N_{\text{phases}})}\)). Fixed times are omitted from \(W\).
  • State Matrix (\(X^{(p)}\)) for phase \(p\): Dimensions \(n_x^{(p)} \times (n^{(p)} + 1)\), flattened into a column vector containing all states across all nodes in phase \(p\):
\[X^{(p)} = \begin{bmatrix} x_0^{(p)} & x_1^{(p)} & \dots & x_{n^{(p)}}^{(p)} \end{bmatrix}\]
  • Control Matrix (\(U^{(p)}\)) for phase \(p\): Dimensions \(n_u^{(p)} \times n^{(p)}\), flattened into a column vector containing control inputs across all intervals in phase \(p\):
\[U^{(p)} = \begin{bmatrix} u_0^{(p)} & u_1^{(p)} & \dots & u_{n^{(p)}-1}^{(p)} \end{bmatrix}\]

items.title: C. Objective Function Discretization
items.text:
The continuous cost functional is discretized by summing the approximated integrals (Lagrange terms) and terminal costs (Mayer terms) across all phases:

\[J_{\text{NLP}}(W) = \sum_{p=1}^{N_{\text{phases}}} \left( \frac{t_f^{(p)} - t_0^{(p)}}{n^{(p)}} \sum_{k=0}^{n^{(p)}-1} L^{(p)}(t_k^{(p)}, x_k^{(p)}, u_k^{(p)}) + E^{(p)}(t_0^{(p)}, t_f^{(p)}, x_0^{(p)}, x_{n^{(p)}}^{(p)}) \right)\]

(Note: Depending on the chosen numerical quadrature rule—such as trapezoidal or Simpson's rule—appropriate quadrature weights replace the uniform interval scaling factor).

items.title: D. Constraint Vector (\(G(W)\)) Structure
items.text:
All constraints across all phases are stacked vertically into a single global vector \(G(W)\) bounded by lower and upper limits (\(G_{lb} \leq G(W) \leq G_{ub}\)):

  1. Phase Boundary / Endpoint Constraints: Evaluated at the start and end of each phase \(p\):
\[G_{\text{event}}^{(p)} = e^{(p)}(t_0^{(p)}, t_f^{(p)}, x_0^{(p)}, x_{n^{(p)}}^{(p)}), \quad e_{lb}^{(p)} \leq G_{\text{event}}^{(p)} \leq e_{ub}^{(p)}\]
  1. Inter-Phase Linkage Constraints: Enforces boundary, transition, or matching conditions between connected phases (e.g., state continuity \(x_f^{(p)} = x_0^{(p+1)}\) or time synchronization):
\[G_{\text{link}} = g\left(\{t_0^{(p)}, t_f^{(p)}, x_0^{(p)}, x_{n^{(p)}}^{(p)}\}_{p=1}^{N_{\text{phases}}}\right), \quad g_{lb} \leq G_{\text{link}} \leq g_{ub}\]
  1. System Dynamics / Defect Constraints: Enforces physical consistency between nodes using the chosen integration method independently for each phase \(p\) (e.g., \(x_{k+1}^{(p)} - x_k^{(p)} - \Delta t^{(p)} f^{(p)}(\cdot) = 0\)):
\[G_{\text{dyn}}^{(p)} = \text{Defects}^{(p)}(X^{(p)}, U^{(p)}, t^{(p)}) = 0, \quad \forall p \in \{1, \dots, N_{\text{phases}}\}\]
  1. Path Constraints: Evaluated across all grid nodes \(k = 0, \dots, n^{(p)}\) for each phase \(p\) (using zero-order hold extension for control inputs at the final node):
\[G_{\text{path}}^{(p)} = \begin{bmatrix} h^{(p)}(t_0^{(p)}, x_0^{(p)}, u_0^{(p)}) \\ \vdots \\ h^{(p)}(t_{n^{(p)}}^{(p)}, x_{n^{(p)}}^{(p)}, u_{n^{(p)}-1}^{(p)}) \end{bmatrix}, \quad h_{lb}^{(p)} \leq G_{\text{path}}^{(p)} \leq h_{ub}^{(p)}\]

items.title: Assembled Final Multiphase NLP Formulation
items.text:
Combining the discretized objective function, stacked multiphase constraints, and decision vector bounds, the fully assembled Nonlinear Program (NLP) solved by CasADi and IPOPT takes the following standard mathematical form:

\[\min_{W} \quad J_{\text{NLP}}(W)\]

Subject to the composite constraints:

\[G_{lb} \leq G(W) \leq G_{ub}\]

where the global constraint vector \(G(W)\) aggregates the boundary, linkage, dynamics (defects), and path constraints across all phases:

\[G(W) = \begin{bmatrix} e^{(1)}(t_0^{(1)}, t_f^{(1)}, x_0^{(1)}, x_{n^{(1)}}^{(1)}) \\ \vdots \\ e^{(N_{\text{phases}})}(t_0^{(N_{\text{phases}})}, t_f^{(N_{\text{phases}})}, x_0^{(N_{\text{phases}})}, x_{n^{(N_{\text{phases}})}}^{(N_{\text{phases}})}) \\ g(\{t_0^{(p)}, t_f^{(p)}, x_0^{(p)}, x_{n^{(p)}}^{(p)}\}_{p=1}^{N_{\text{phases}}}) \\ \text{Defects}^{(1)}(X^{(1)}, U^{(1)}, t^{(1)}) \\ \vdots \\ \text{Defects}^{(N_{\text{phases}})}(X^{(N_{\text{phases}})}, U^{(N_{\text{phases}})}, t^{(N_{\text{phases}})}) \\ h^{(1)}(t_0^{(1)}, x_0^{(1)}, u_0^{(1)}) \\ \vdots \\ h^{(N_{\text{phases}})}(t_{n^{(N_{\text{phases}})}}^{(N_{\text{phases}})}, x_{n^{(N_{\text{phases}})}}^{(N_{\text{phases}})}, u_{n^{(N_{\text{phases}})}-1}^{(N_{\text{phases}})}) \end{bmatrix}\]

With corresponding lower and upper constraint bounds:

\[G_{lb} = \begin{bmatrix} e_{lb}^{(1)} \\ \vdots \\ e_{lb}^{(N_{\text{phases}})} \\ g_{lb} \\ \mathbf{0}^{(1)} \\ \vdots \\ \mathbf{0}^{(N_{\text{phases}})} \\ h_{lb}^{(1)} \\ \vdots \\ h_{lb}^{(N_{\text{phases}})} \end{bmatrix}, \quad G_{ub} = \begin{bmatrix} e_{ub}^{(1)} \\ \vdots \\ e_{ub}^{(N_{\text{phases}})} \\ g_{ub} \\ \mathbf{0}^{(1)} \\ \vdots \\ \mathbf{0}^{(N_{\text{phases}})} \\ h_{ub}^{(1)} \\ \vdots \\ h_{ub}^{(N_{\text{phases}})} \end{bmatrix}\]

And subject to simple variable bounds on the global decision vector \(W\):

\[W_{lb} \leq W \leq W_{ub}\]

where:

\[ W = \begin{bmatrix} T_{\text{free}} \\ \text{vec}(X^{(1)}) \\ \text{vec}(U^{(1)}) \\ \vdots \\ \text{vec}(X^{(N_{\text{phases}})}) \\ \text{vec}(U^{(N_{\text{phases}})}) \end{bmatrix}, \quad W_{lb} = \begin{bmatrix} T_{\text{free}, lb} \\ \text{repmat}(x_{lb}^{(1)}, 1, n^{(1)}+1) \\ \text{repmat}(u_{lb}^{(1)}, 1, n^{(1)}) \\ \vdots \\ \text{repmat}(x_{lb}^{(N_{\text{phases}})}, 1, n^{(N_{\text{phases}})}+1) \\ \text{repmat}(u_{lb}^{(N_{\text{phases}})}, 1, n^{(N_{\text{phases}})}) \end{bmatrix}, \quad W_{ub} = \begin{bmatrix} T_{\text{free}, ub} \\ \text{repmat}(x_{ub}^{(1)}, 1, n^{(1)}+1) \\ \text{repmat}(u_{ub}^{(1)}, 1, n^{(1)}) \\ \vdots \\ \text{repmat}(x_{ub}^{(N_{\text{phases}})}, 1, n^{(N_{\text{phases}})}+1) \\ \text{repmat}(u_{ub}^{(N_{\text{phases}})}, 1, n^{(N_{\text{phases}})}) \end{bmatrix} \]

items.title: Discretization & Integration Methods
items.text:
The framework supports flexible transcription strategies where each phase can independently configure its own integration and collocation backend, categorized into Direct Multiple Shooting and Direct Collocation:

  • Direct Multiple Shooting (Explicit & Adaptive Integrators):
  • fw_euler: Forward Euler (explicit 1st-order).
  • exp_mid: Explicit Midpoint (2nd-order Runge-Kutta).
  • rk4: Standard 4th-order Runge-Kutta (via CasADi integrator).
  • cvodes: Adaptive-step ODE/DAE integrator from SUNDIALS (ideal for stiff dynamics).

  • collocation: Implicit collocation polynomials via CasADi.

  • Direct Collocation (Implicit Methods):

  • bw_euler: Backward Euler (implicit 1st-order, highly stable).
  • trap: Trapezoidal collocation (implicit 2nd-order).
  • her_sim: Hermite-Simpson collocation (cubic polynomial approximation).

items.title: Ocp
items.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Source code in pytrajopt\pytrajopt.py 
class Ocp(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True, extra="forbid")
    # dimensions of state control and discretization intervals
    nx: PositiveInt
    nu: PositiveInt
    n: PositiveInt
    # initial and final time
    t0: cs.DM | None = None  # none means free var
    tf: cs.DM | None = None  # none means free var
    # Lagrange (L), Mayer (E), event (e), dynamics (f), path (h) functions
    L: cs.Function | None = None  # none means zero
    E: cs.Function | None = None  # zero
    f: cs.Function
    e: cs.Function
    h: cs.Function | None = None  # optional
    # numerical method for dynamics approximation
    method: dis_methods
    # path constraint bounds
    h_lb: cs.DM | None = None  # optional
    h_ub: cs.DM | None = None  # optional
    # event constraint bounds
    e_lb: cs.DM
    e_ub: cs.DM
    # simple bounds on state and control
    x_lb: cs.DM | None = None  # optional
    x_ub: cs.DM | None = None  # optional
    u_lb: cs.DM | None = None  # optional
    u_ub: cs.DM | None = None  # optional
    # bounds in initial and final time if free
    t0_lb: cs.DM | None = None  # optional
    t0_ub: cs.DM | None = None  # optional
    tf_lb: cs.DM | None = None  # optional
    tf_ub: cs.DM | None = None  # optional
    # scale
    J_s: cs.DM | None = None
    x_s: cs.DM | None = None
    u_s: cs.DM | None = None
    e_s: cs.DM | None = None
    h_s: cs.DM | None = None
    t_s: cs.DM | None = None
    # offset
    x_o: cs.DM | None = None
    u_o: cs.DM | None = None
    t_o: cs.DM | None = None
    # obj tuple[cs.DM,cs.DM] | None (1,0)
    # constriant
    # variables

    @field_validator("f", "L", "h")
    @classmethod
    def path_func_validate(cls, f: cs.Function) -> cs.Function:
        """

        Check input and output structure of path function

        f(t,x,u) -> (,1)


        Parameters
        ----------
        f : cs.Function |None


        Returns
        -------
        cs.Function|none

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            number of inputs mismatch
        ValueError
            number of outputs mismatch
        ValueError
            output is not a column vector
        """

        if f is not None:
            if f.n_in() != 3:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Expected (t,x,u) for {f.name()} as input but received only ({f.n_in()}) inputs"
                )

            if f.n_out() != 1:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Expected a single output for {f.name()} but received ({f.n_out()})"
                )

            if f.size_out(0)[1] != 1:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"functions passed must return column vector but received {f.size_out(0)}"
                )

        return f

    @field_validator("E", "e")
    @classmethod
    def event_func_validate(cls, f: cs.Function | None) -> cs.Function | None:
        """

        Check input and output structure of event function

        f(t0,tf,x0,xf) -> (,1)

        Parameters
        ----------
        f : cs.Function|None


        Returns
        -------
        cs.Function|None

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            number of inputs mismatch
        ValueError
            number of outputs mismatch
        ValueError
            output is not a column vector
        """

        if f is not None:
            if f.n_in() != 4:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Expected (t0,tf,x0,xf) for {f.name()} as input but received only ({f.n_in()}) inputs"
                )

            if f.n_out() != 1:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Expected a single output for {f.name()} but received({f.n_out()})"
                )

            if f.size_out(0)[1] != 1:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"functions passed must return column vector but received {f.size_out(0)}"
                )

        return f

    def get_path_funcs(
        self,
    ) -> tuple[cs.Function | None, cs.Function, cs.Function | None]:
        """
        get all path functions as a tuple (L,f,h)

        Returns
        -------
        tuple[cs.Function|None,cs.Function,cs.Function|None]
            collection of function or None objects
        """
        return (self.L, self.f, self.h)

    def get_event_funcs(self) -> tuple[cs.Function | None, cs.Function]:
        """
        get all evemt functions as a tuple (E,e)

        Returns
        -------
        tuple[cs.Function|None,cs.Function,cs.Function|None]
            collection of function or None objects
        """
        return (self.E, self.e)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_Ocp(self) -> "Ocp":
        """
        Once basic check on certain fields which hold constants and functions
        are complete, additional checks are done to

        1. check dimension consistency of path and input functions
        2. check shape of dynamics, Lagrange and Mayer terms
        3. validate bounds for variables and constraints

        Returns
        -------
        Ocp
            Trajectory optimization object
        """

        self.path_func_ip_check(self.get_path_funcs())
        self.event_func_ip_check(self.get_event_funcs())
        self.func_shapes()
        self.check_lb_ub()
        self.check_scale_offset()

        return self

    def func_shapes(self) -> None:
        """
        check shape of dynamics, Lagrange and Mayer terms

        Returns
        -------
        None

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            dynamics vector dont match state dimension
        ValueError
            Lagrange/Mayer are not scalars
        """

        # f is mandatory vector
        if self.f.size_out(0) != (self.nx, 1):
            raise ValueError(
                f"dynamics function ({self.f.name()}) must return a {(self.nx, 1)} vector but received {self.f.size_out(0)}"
            )

        for name, func in zip(["Lagrange", "Mayer"], [self.L, self.E]):
            # L and E are optional (None sets them to zero)
            if func is not None and func.size_out(0) != (1, 1):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{name} function ({func.name()}) must return a scalar vector but received {func.size_out(0)}"
                )

    def path_func_ip_check(self, funcs) -> None:
        """

        check the size of each input of path function

        Parameters
        ----------
        funcs : _type_
            collection of path functions

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            dimension of the path  input variables does not match with dimensions of time, state and control
        """
        inputs = ["t", "x", "u"]
        for func in funcs:
            if func is not None:
                for i, j in enumerate([(1, 1), (self.nx, 1), (self.nu, 1)]):
                    if func.size_in(i) != j:
                        raise ValueError(
                            f"Dimension of {inputs[i]} must be {j} but received {func.size_in(i)} for {func.name()}"
                        )

    def event_func_ip_check(self, funcs) -> None:
        """

        check the size of each input of event function

        Parameters
        ----------
        funcs : _type_
            collection of event functions

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            dimension of the event input variables does not match with dimensions of time, state at initial and final points
        """
        inputs = ["t0", "tf", "x0", "xf"]
        for func in funcs:
            if func is not None:
                for i, j in enumerate([(1, 1), (1, 1), (self.nx, 1), (self.nx, 1)]):
                    if func.size_in(i) != j:
                        raise ValueError(
                            f"Dimension of {inputs[i]} must be {j} but received{func.size_in(i)} for {func.name()}"
                        )

    def check_lb_ub(self) -> None:
        """
        1. assign defaults simple bounds for state control and time
        2. checks if bounds are valid

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            bounds set for fixed time t0/tf
        ValueError
            final time < initial time
        ValueError
            bounds set for no path constraints
        ValueError
            bounds not set for path constraint
        """

        # process defaults
        # none implies unbounded
        # if not none keep it as it is
        simple = {
            "x_lb": (self.x_lb, (self.nx, 1)),
            "x_ub": (self.x_ub, (self.nx, 1)),
            "u_lb": (self.u_lb, (self.nu, 1)),
            "u_ub": (self.u_ub, (self.nu, 1)),
        }

        for name, obj_and_shape in simple.items():
            if obj_and_shape[0] is None:
                if "_lb" in name:
                    c = -1
                else:
                    c = 1
                # override nones to +/- inf
                setattr(self, name, c * cs.DM.inf() * cs.DM.ones(obj_and_shape[1]))
            # match shapes of x and u, detect nan
            Ocp.check_shape(
                name=name, vec=getattr(self, name), known_shape=obj_and_shape[1]
            )
            Ocp.check_nan(name=name, vec=getattr(self, name))

        Ocp.check_lb_le_ub(self.x_lb, self.x_ub, "x")
        Ocp.check_lb_le_ub(self.u_lb, self.u_ub, "u")

        time = {
            "t0_lb": (self.t0_lb, (1, 1)),
            "t0_ub": (self.t0_ub, (1, 1)),
            "tf_lb": (self.tf_lb, (1, 1)),
            "tf_ub": (self.tf_ub, (1, 1)),
        }

        for name, obj_and_shape in time.items():
            # free
            if getattr(self, name[:2]) is None:
                # set default to unassigned time bounds
                if obj_and_shape[0] is None:
                    if "_lb" in name:
                        # positive time
                        setattr(self, name, cs.DM(1e-8))
                    else:
                        # no upper limit
                        setattr(self, name, cs.DM.inf())
                else:
                    # user defined - check quality of data and its shape
                    Ocp.check_shape(
                        name=name, vec=obj_and_shape[0], known_shape=obj_and_shape[1]
                    )
                    Ocp.check_nan(name=name, vec=obj_and_shape[0])
            else:
                # t0/tf are fixed
                if obj_and_shape[0] is not None:
                    raise ValueError(f"Cannot set bounds to fixed variable {name[:2]}")

        if self.t0 is None:
            Ocp.check_lb_le_ub(self.t0_lb, self.t0_ub, "t0")
        if self.tf is None:
            Ocp.check_lb_le_ub(self.tf_lb, self.tf_ub, "tf")

        # fixed t0,tf -> tf>t0
        if self.tf is not None and self.t0 is not None and self.t0 > self.tf:
            raise ValueError(
                f"final time must be greater than initial time but t0 ({self.t0})> tf ({self.tf})"
            )

        if self.h is None:
            if self.h_lb is not None or self.h_ub is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Cannot set bounds h_lb or h_ub when path constraint h is not set (None)"
                )
        else:
            for name, bound in zip(["h_lb", "h_ub"], [self.h_lb, self.h_ub]):
                if bound is None:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"{name} not set for h. Update {name} with valid bounds vector"
                    )
                Ocp.check_nan(vec=bound, name=name)
            Ocp.check_constraint_shapes(self.h, self.h_lb, self.h_ub, self.h.name())
            Ocp.check_lb_le_ub(self.h_lb, self.h_ub, "h")

        Ocp.check_nan(vec=self.e_lb, name="e_lb")
        Ocp.check_nan(vec=self.e_ub, name="e_ub")
        Ocp.check_constraint_shapes(self.e, self.e_lb, self.e_ub, self.e.name())
        Ocp.check_lb_le_ub(self.e_lb, self.e_ub, "e")

    def check_scale_offset(self):

        # assign defaults
        # same as calling them without scaling them

        names = ["J_s", "x_s", "u_s", "e_s"]
        shapes = [(1, 1), (self.nx, 1), (self.nu, 1), self.e.size_out(0)]

        for name, shape in zip(names, shapes):
            if getattr(self, name) is None:
                setattr(self, name, cs.DM.ones(shape))
            Ocp.check_nan(getattr(self, name), name)
            Ocp.check_shape(getattr(self, name), shape, name)

        names = ["x_o", "u_o"]
        shapes = [(self.nx, 1), (self.nu, 1)]

        for name, shape in zip(names, shapes):
            if getattr(self, name) is None:
                setattr(self, name, cs.DM.zeros(shape))
            Ocp.check_nan(getattr(self, name), name)
            Ocp.check_shape(getattr(self, name), shape, name)

        if self.J_s is not None and self.J_s <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                "Objective scaling factor must be positive. Negative scaling not allowed"
            )

        if self.t0 is None or self.tf is None:
            names = ["t_s", "t_o"]
            defaults = [cs.DM(1), cs.DM(0)]
            for name, default in zip(names, defaults):
                if getattr(self, name) is None:
                    setattr(self, name, default)
                Ocp.check_nan(getattr(self, name), name)
                Ocp.check_shape(getattr(self, name), (1, 1), name)
        else:
            if self.t_s is not None or self.t_o is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Cannot set scales for time variables when both t0 and tf are fixed"
                )

        if self.h is not None:
            if self.h_s is None:
                self.h_s = cs.DM.ones(self.h.size_out(0))
            Ocp.check_nan(self.h_s, "h_s")
            Ocp.check_shape(self.h_s, self.h.size_out(0), "h_s")
        else:
            if self.h_s is not None:
                raise ValueError("Cannot set scales for OCP with no path constraints")

    @classmethod
    def check_constraint_shapes(cls, g: cs.Function, lb: cs.DM, ub: cs.DM, name: str):
        """
        constraint shape must match with bounds

        Parameters
        ----------
        g : cs.Function
            constraint function
        lb : cs.DM
            lower bound
        ub : cs.DM
            upper bound
        name : str
            function name

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            bounds and constraint function dimension dont match
        """
        if not (lb.shape == ub.shape == g.size_out(0)):
            raise ValueError(
                f"The shape of bounds ({name}_lb={lb.shape},{name}_ub={ub.shape}) provided does not match with output of function ({name}={g.size_out(0)})"
            )

    @classmethod
    def check_nan(cls, vec: cs.DM, name: str):
        """
        check of vector contains NaN values

        prevent corruption of data

        Parameters
        ----------
        vec : cs.DM
            constant vector
        name : str
            name

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            Nan was there in vec
        """
        if np.isnan(vec.full()).any():
            raise ValueError(f"{name} cannot have NaN")

    @classmethod
    def check_lb_le_ub(cls, lb: cs.DM, ub: cs.DM, name: str) -> None:
        """
        upper bound must be greater than lower bounds vector

        Parameters
        ----------
        lb : cs.DM
            lower bound
        ub : cs.DM
            upper bounds
        name : str
            name of constraint function

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            lower bound greater than upper bound
        """
        if np.any(lb.full() > ub.full()):
            raise ValueError(
                f"lower must be <= upper bound for {name} but {name}_lb ({lb}) > {name}_ub ({ub})"
            )

    @classmethod
    def check_shape(cls, vec: cs.DM, known_shape: tuple, name):
        """
        compare shape of matrix with true/expected shape

        Parameters
        ----------
        vec : cs.DM
            constant vector
        known_shape : tuple
            true shape of vector
        name : _type_
            name of the vector used

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            shape of vector not matching with the truth
        """
        if vec.shape != known_shape:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{name} is incorrect shape. Expected {known_shape}, got {vec.shape}"
            )

def check_lb_ub(self) -> None:
    """
    1. assign defaults simple bounds for state control and time
    2. checks if bounds are valid

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        bounds set for fixed time t0/tf
    ValueError
        final time < initial time
    ValueError
        bounds set for no path constraints
    ValueError
        bounds not set for path constraint
    """

    # process defaults
    # none implies unbounded
    # if not none keep it as it is
    simple = {
        "x_lb": (self.x_lb, (self.nx, 1)),
        "x_ub": (self.x_ub, (self.nx, 1)),
        "u_lb": (self.u_lb, (self.nu, 1)),
        "u_ub": (self.u_ub, (self.nu, 1)),
    }

    for name, obj_and_shape in simple.items():
        if obj_and_shape[0] is None:
            if "_lb" in name:
                c = -1
            else:
                c = 1
            # override nones to +/- inf
            setattr(self, name, c * cs.DM.inf() * cs.DM.ones(obj_and_shape[1]))
        # match shapes of x and u, detect nan
        Ocp.check_shape(
            name=name, vec=getattr(self, name), known_shape=obj_and_shape[1]
        )
        Ocp.check_nan(name=name, vec=getattr(self, name))

    Ocp.check_lb_le_ub(self.x_lb, self.x_ub, "x")
    Ocp.check_lb_le_ub(self.u_lb, self.u_ub, "u")

    time = {
        "t0_lb": (self.t0_lb, (1, 1)),
        "t0_ub": (self.t0_ub, (1, 1)),
        "tf_lb": (self.tf_lb, (1, 1)),
        "tf_ub": (self.tf_ub, (1, 1)),
    }

    for name, obj_and_shape in time.items():
        # free
        if getattr(self, name[:2]) is None:
            # set default to unassigned time bounds
            if obj_and_shape[0] is None:
                if "_lb" in name:
                    # positive time
                    setattr(self, name, cs.DM(1e-8))
                else:
                    # no upper limit
                    setattr(self, name, cs.DM.inf())
            else:
                # user defined - check quality of data and its shape
                Ocp.check_shape(
                    name=name, vec=obj_and_shape[0], known_shape=obj_and_shape[1]
                )
                Ocp.check_nan(name=name, vec=obj_and_shape[0])
        else:
            # t0/tf are fixed
            if obj_and_shape[0] is not None:
                raise ValueError(f"Cannot set bounds to fixed variable {name[:2]}")

    if self.t0 is None:
        Ocp.check_lb_le_ub(self.t0_lb, self.t0_ub, "t0")
    if self.tf is None:
        Ocp.check_lb_le_ub(self.tf_lb, self.tf_ub, "tf")

    # fixed t0,tf -> tf>t0
    if self.tf is not None and self.t0 is not None and self.t0 > self.tf:
        raise ValueError(
            f"final time must be greater than initial time but t0 ({self.t0})> tf ({self.tf})"
        )

    if self.h is None:
        if self.h_lb is not None or self.h_ub is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Cannot set bounds h_lb or h_ub when path constraint h is not set (None)"
            )
    else:
        for name, bound in zip(["h_lb", "h_ub"], [self.h_lb, self.h_ub]):
            if bound is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{name} not set for h. Update {name} with valid bounds vector"
                )
            Ocp.check_nan(vec=bound, name=name)
        Ocp.check_constraint_shapes(self.h, self.h_lb, self.h_ub, self.h.name())
        Ocp.check_lb_le_ub(self.h_lb, self.h_ub, "h")

    Ocp.check_nan(vec=self.e_lb, name="e_lb")
    Ocp.check_nan(vec=self.e_ub, name="e_ub")
    Ocp.check_constraint_shapes(self.e, self.e_lb, self.e_ub, self.e.name())
    Ocp.check_lb_le_ub(self.e_lb, self.e_ub, "e")

@field_validator("E", "e")
@classmethod
def event_func_validate(cls, f: cs.Function | None) -> cs.Function | None:
    """

    Check input and output structure of event function

    f(t0,tf,x0,xf) -> (,1)

    Parameters
    ----------
    f : cs.Function|None


    Returns
    -------
    cs.Function|None

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        number of inputs mismatch
    ValueError
        number of outputs mismatch
    ValueError
        output is not a column vector
    """

    if f is not None:
        if f.n_in() != 4:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected (t0,tf,x0,xf) for {f.name()} as input but received only ({f.n_in()}) inputs"
            )

        if f.n_out() != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected a single output for {f.name()} but received({f.n_out()})"
            )

        if f.size_out(0)[1] != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"functions passed must return column vector but received {f.size_out(0)}"
            )

    return f

def func_shapes(self) -> None:
    """
    check shape of dynamics, Lagrange and Mayer terms

    Returns
    -------
    None

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        dynamics vector dont match state dimension
    ValueError
        Lagrange/Mayer are not scalars
    """

    # f is mandatory vector
    if self.f.size_out(0) != (self.nx, 1):
        raise ValueError(
            f"dynamics function ({self.f.name()}) must return a {(self.nx, 1)} vector but received {self.f.size_out(0)}"
        )

    for name, func in zip(["Lagrange", "Mayer"], [self.L, self.E]):
        # L and E are optional (None sets them to zero)
        if func is not None and func.size_out(0) != (1, 1):
            raise ValueError(
                f"{name} function ({func.name()}) must return a scalar vector but received {func.size_out(0)}"
            )

@model_validator(mode="after")
def validate_Ocp(self) -> "Ocp":
    """
    Once basic check on certain fields which hold constants and functions
    are complete, additional checks are done to

    1. check dimension consistency of path and input functions
    2. check shape of dynamics, Lagrange and Mayer terms
    3. validate bounds for variables and constraints

    Returns
    -------
    Ocp
        Trajectory optimization object
    """

    self.path_func_ip_check(self.get_path_funcs())
    self.event_func_ip_check(self.get_event_funcs())
    self.func_shapes()
    self.check_lb_ub()
    self.check_scale_offset()

    return self

class casadi_integrator(BaseModel):
    # provides access to casadi integrators
    model_config = ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True, extra="forbid")
    plugin: Literal["cvodes", "collocation", "rk"] = "rk"
    plugin_options: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)
    nx: int
    nu: int
    path: list[cs.SX]
    f: cs.SX
    _scaled_ode: dict[str, cs.SX] = PrivateAttr(default_factory=dict)

    @field_validator("path")
    @classmethod
    def check_length(cls, path: list[cs.SX]) -> list[cs.SX]:
        """

        length of path list must be 3 [t,x,u]

        Parameters
        ----------
        path : list[cs.SX]
            the path variables

        Returns
        -------
        list[cs.SX]
            validated path variables

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            length of the list is not 3
        """
        if len(path) != 3:
            raise ValueError(
                f"t,x,u must be present in path. Recived {len(path)} expected 3"
            )
        return path

    @field_validator("f")
    @classmethod
    def check_column(cls, f: cs.SX) -> cs.SX:
        """

        the dynamics vector must be a column vector

        Parameters
        ----------
        f : cs.SX
            xd=f(t,x,u)

        Returns
        -------
        cs.SX
            validated f vector

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            if a tow vector or matrix is passed
        """
        if f.shape[1] != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"f must be a column vector but received f of shape {f.shape}"
            )
        return f

    def __eq__(self, other: str) -> bool:
        """
        casadi_integrator=='casadi_integrator' must return true

        this functionality added to keep Ocp code clean

        Parameters
        ----------
        other : str
            string to be compared against

        Returns
        -------
        bool
            truth value
        """
        # If the other object is a string, check if it matches the class name
        if isinstance(other, str):
            return self.__class__.__name__ == other

        # Fallback to standard comparison for other object types
        return super().__eq__(other)

    @classmethod
    def get_scaled_dynamics(cls, path: list, f: cs.SX) -> dict[str, cs.SX]:
        """
        transform time from [t0,tf]->[0,1] (tau)

        t0 tf are parameters in the ode (constants along the control vector)

        helps to reuse casadi integrator object

        Parameters
        ----------
        path : []
            path variables [t,x,u]
        f : cs.SX
            ode expression [xd=f(t,x,u)]

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str,cs.SX]
            transformed ode in a dict
        """

        t0s = cs.SX.sym("t0s")
        tfs = cs.SX.sym("tfs")
        tau = cs.SX.sym("tau")
        t = t0s + (tfs - t0s) * tau
        f_scaled = cs.transform((tfs - t0s) * cs.substitute(f, path[0], t))
        ode_s = {
            "t": tau,
            "x": path[1],
            "p": cs.vertcat(path[2], t0s, tfs),
            "ode": f_scaled,
        }
        return ode_s

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def generate_ode_dict(self) -> "casadi_integrator":
        """
        casadi.integrator compatible dict generation

        Returns
        -------
        casadi_integrator
            all objects needed to create a casadi integrator

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            shape mismatch of path variables
        """
        syms_shapes = [(1, 1), (self.nx, 1), (self.nu, 1), (self.nx, 1)]
        syms = self.path + [self.f]
        for name, known_shape, object in zip(["t", "x", "u", "f"], syms_shapes, syms):
            if object.shape != known_shape:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{name} is a {known_shape} vector but received {object.shape}"
                )

        self._scaled_ode = casadi_integrator.get_scaled_dynamics(self.path, self.f)

        return self

    # If the other object is a string, check if it matches the class name

@classmethod
def get_scaled_dynamics(cls, path: list, f: cs.SX) -> dict[str, cs.SX]:
    """
    transform time from [t0,tf]->[0,1] (tau)

    t0 tf are parameters in the ode (constants along the control vector)

    helps to reuse casadi integrator object

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : []
        path variables [t,x,u]
    f : cs.SX
        ode expression [xd=f(t,x,u)]

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str,cs.SX]
        transformed ode in a dict
    """

    t0s = cs.SX.sym("t0s")
    tfs = cs.SX.sym("tfs")
    tau = cs.SX.sym("tau")
    t = t0s + (tfs - t0s) * tau
    f_scaled = cs.transform((tfs - t0s) * cs.substitute(f, path[0], t))
    ode_s = {
        "t": tau,
        "x": path[1],
        "p": cs.vertcat(path[2], t0s, tfs),
        "ode": f_scaled,
    }
    return ode_s
